sla_summary: Customer requests 99.95% uptime for Dedicated cluster; proposed credit schedule: 5% credit if uptime <99.95 and >=99.9, 15% if <99.9 and >=99.5, 40% if <99.5. Maintenance windows limited to Sunday 02:00-04:00 PST with 72h notice. Support P1 response target requested = 1 hour, P2 = 4 hours, P3 = 24 hours. Redwood proposed 99.9% baseline, monthly maintenance twice/month windows 02:00-04:00 local, and standard support P1=2 hours; negotiation ongoing.
sla_negotiation_points: Uptime target: Rivermark insists on 99.95% — Redwood's standard enterprise SLA is 99.9%; gap analysis required.
Credit schedule: customer wants steeper credits earlier (higher percentage at smaller deltas). Legal flags service credit cap and recovery process.
Maintenance windows: customer requires single monthly window in PST off-peak; Redwood prefers templated windows that vary by region — compromise needed.
Support SLAs: Rivermark demands 1h P1 response and named escalation contacts; Redwood to confirm 24/7 coverage and on-call rotations.
Throughput guarantees: commit to sustained tokens/sec and concurrent sessions; exact metric & measurement method to be defined in SLA appendix.
Performance remediation: require runbook for on-call mitigation, automatic fallback to smaller model variants, and guaranteed time-to-resolution targets for P1/P2 incidents.
Maintenance credits vs incident credits: clarify stacking rules and credit calculation formula for partial outages.
Data residency & KMS: ensure contractual guarantees for key management and US-only residency for customer data in production.
Reserved GPU planning: initial commit 8x A10-equivalent, scale to 16x after Q3; include explicit lead times for procurement and capacity reservation.
Reporting: weekly token/latency reports during ramp period and post-cutover monthly SLA reports with per-route breakdown.
